title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'loop equation' notes Grothendieck works with a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M (a twisted 2x2 matrix algebra) over a base S, with sections rho and sigma and a unipotent section eps_0 = 1 + N_0, where N_0^2 = 0. He wants to identify a certain S-scheme X_{rho,sigma}, defined earlier (around (56)), with a twisted form of a familiar group.

Previous page. On the previous page he first tried the full stabilizer B_0 of the nilpotent N_0. In the split case B_0 is the upper-triangular Borel {(p, l; 0, q)}. He decomposes det u = p(u) q(u) intrinsically via u N_0 u^{-1} = (p/q) N_0. He decides the 'good' group is not the one cut out by q^2 = 1, but B'_0 = {q = 1} = {(p, l; 0, 1)}.

This page.
1. B'_0 is a smooth group scheme (the reading 'libre' is surely 'lisse'). It sits in a canonical exact sequence 1 -> L_0 -> B'_0 -> G_m -> 1. Here L_0 is the unipotent radical, a twisted form of G_a, and the map to G_m is det (= p since q = 1). So B'_0 is a twisted form of the affine group Aff_1 = G_a ⋊ G_m, i.e. of the Borel subgroup of PGL_2.
2. (75) B'_0 ∩ G_m = {1}, with G_m the central scalars: a scalar lambda lies in B'_0 only if q = lambda = 1. Hence B'_0 maps monomorphically to M^*/G_m = PGL(M). Consequently the morphism B'_0 -> X_{rho,sigma} induced by (56) is a monomorphism.
3. To prove it is an isomorphism, 'by general principles' it suffices to check surjectivity on points with values in algebraically closed fields. Behind this is the standard EGA IV-type criterion: a monomorphism locally of finite presentation which is flat (e.g. between smooth S-schemes of the same relative dimension) and surjective is an isomorphism. He possibly adds a simplifying hypothesis on S; the parenthesis is illegible. The details are left out.

Remark at the bottom. Via condition (40 bis), the data can be reparametrised by a unipotent section eps_1 = 1 + N_1 (N_1^2 = 0) and the section rho, with sigma deduced from them. The next page makes this explicit: sigma = -eps_1^{-1} rho, i.e. rho + sigma = N_1 rho.

Purpose. This re-parametrises the pair (rho, sigma) of 2x2 'monodromy-like' elements with one unipotent relation. It describes the symmetry or moduli scheme of such configurations as a twisted affine group.
errors: 'groupe qui est libre' should almost certainly read 'lisse' (smooth); a free group makes no sense here.
The sequence is numbered (74) again, duplicating (74) of the previous page; presumably (74 bis).

The surjectivity-on-geometric-points criterion needs flatness or smoothness and finite presentation (e.g. same relative dimension, smooth target). Grothendieck invokes 'principes généraux' without stating these hypotheses, and the verification is explicitly skipped.

ideas.what: The 'good' stabilizer group: the Borel of PGL_2 realised as {q(u)=1} inside the stabilizer of a nilpotent in an Azumaya algebra, a twisted form of Aff_1, with exact sequence 1->L_0->B'_0->G_m->1
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup of PGL(M) / twisted affine group G_a ⋊ G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA3 theory of reductive group schemes)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (Borel subgroups of reductive group schemes)

ideas.what: A monomorphism of finitely presented smooth S-schemes that is surjective on geometric points is an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: EGA IV criterion for monomorphisms (17.9 type)

ideas.what: Reparametrising (rho, sigma) by rho and a unipotent eps_1 = 1+N_1 with sigma = -eps_1^{-1} rho, so that rho+sigma = N_1 rho differs from rank one by a transvection
ideas.modern_name: hypergeometric-type pair (Levelt): rho and -sigma differ by a pseudo-reflection

missed.claim: The remark (completed on the next page) parametrises the rank-2 data by rho and a transvection eps_1 = -rho sigma^{-1}, i.e. rho and -sigma differ by a rank-one (unipotent) pseudo-reflection. Over a general base S in Azumaya form, this is the Levelt/Beukers–Heckman hypergeometric condition. Grothendieck does not name it, but his scheme-theoretic, Azumaya-twisted treatment of this configuration within the 'loop equation' study of genus-0 Teichmüller data is not something I know in the literature.
missed.quote: l'existence d'une section ε_1 = 1+tN_1 (N_1^2=0) unipotente de Sta(M), et d'une section ρ, et que σ n'en est déduit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links his anabelian/Teichmüller loop-equation work to rigid local systems and hypergeometric monodromy groups over arbitrary bases. The link is suggestive, but the content on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine group-scheme verifications (smooth Borel of PGL_2, trivial intersection with the centre, an isomorphism criterion). Only the closing remark hints at a hypergeometric-type parametrisation, which is developed on the next page.
